negative_reviews.author: Suelen Mathias Borges
negative_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, we didn’t even get the chance to try the food, so I can’t comment on that. However, the customer service was the worst I’ve ever experienced.

From what I saw in the two minutes we were there, it’s a beautiful venue in a great location. We decided to visit after seeing it advertised and my partner purchased a Groupon voucher, as neither of us had been there before.

When we arrived, we immediately told the receptionist that we had a Groupon voucher. She welcomed us, did a big show with a drum showed us to a table, and said everything was fine. A few moments later, another member of staff came over and told us we couldn’t use the Groupon voucher on weekends, that could be totally avoided.

The frustrating part is that this restriction wasn’t made clear on Groupon, and if weekends weren’t eligible, the receptionist should have told us before seating us. Instead, we were seated, which was embarrassing and completely avoidable.

The restaurant looks lovely, and although the menu apparently nice, we were happy to give it a try. Sadly, the poor customer service completely changed our impression.

Losing two customers means losing much more than that. We won’t be returning, and unfortunately we can’t recommend the restaurant to our friends, family, or clients. A simple apology doesn’t make up for being treated so dismissively.

I hope the management takes this feedback on board and invests in better staff training and clearer communication regarding promotional offers. This experience wasn’t just about the Groupon voucher, it was about how we were treated.

negative_reviews.author: Y.K W
negative_reviews.text: The food and environment were good. However, it seemed that the waiters were not very welcoming towards Asian customers, even though they themselves were Asian. We felt that there was a different attitude in the way we were treated compared with local customers.

negative_reviews.author: S X
negative_reviews.text:
The staff were friendly and the restaurant was clean, so no complaints there. However, the food was a major disappointment, especially given the prices.

Everything arrived so quickly that it felt less like a restaurant meal and more like pre-prepared food being assembled. The ramen lacked the depth, freshness, and attention to detail I would expect from a place specializing in Japanese cuisine. The broth tasted generic and lacked the richness of a properly cooked stock, while the noodles and toppings felt highly standardized and pre-portioned.

What also struck me was that I couldn't see any real kitchen operation, which only reinforced the impression that much of the food was prepared elsewhere and simply finished on-site.

The biggest surprise, however, was the rating. After eating here, I genuinely struggled to understand how this place scores so highly. Perhaps many customers are drawn to the Japanese branding, trendy atmosphere, or fast service, but based on food quality alone, I found it very ordinary.

negative_reviews.author: cc z
negative_reviews.text: Make me pay before giving out the bill, very unprofessional. Not impressed, definitely not worth the 10% service fee, which was added to the bill.

negative_reviews.author: Sam Tran
negative_reviews.text:
If you’re after decent food this place is a good bet. However, if you’re looking for a genuine good experience you’ll be disappointed.
The setting is nice and the music playlist is well put together but that’s about it.

The Ton Kotsu was delicious and worth ordering.
The pumpkin croquettes were oddly oily.
The Chicken Katsu Curry was pretty standard but it was nice. A miso soup was supposed to complement the curry but we didn’t realise it until after the meal and we mentioned it.  No apology was given and we left feeling like we were at fault and there was no accountability from the team.
The customer service was terrible.

Organisation and communication definitely aren’t their strong suits and I’m still trying to figure out what they are.
Surprisingly, they cooperated with some free meals after we mentioned we waited over 30 minutes as per the lunch deal policy. That certainly softened the blow.

I love Japanese food and culture, but this was far from it. And you should stay far from it also.

negative_reviews.author: Joanna Carlos
negative_reviews.text:
The food is satisfactory, because it was far far more tastier and creamier before than today. It is still tasty and far better than the others out there.
Atmosphere today too is a bit not conducive for eating because the other table’s children are all around out table.
Service though of Giovana is brilliant. She has accomodated us very kindly and entertained our concern on time and acted immediately. She was all helpful all throughout the meal.
Kudos to the chef as well for dealing with the order that we had issue about.
Overall, we will still recommend the place and the meal. We will still come back for more.

negative_reviews.author: Aliasger Bharmal
negative_reviews.text:
Giovana was very welcoming and clearly explained the menu. Took into account of our allergies and always had a pleasant smile.

The restaurant has a pleasant atmosphere.

negative_reviews.author: Aris Alcantara
negative_reviews.text: They promised that if we don’t get our food within 30 minutes it will be free already. Our takoyaki didn’t come even before we had our bill. That’s a total of more than 1hour of wait. Nobody even apologised or acknowledged that the service/food was late. The waiters were very passive. No urgency at all! negative_reviews.author: Foodie girl
negative_reviews.text:
偽寿司屋です。おすすめしません。
美味しくない。日本食で働いておいてアジア人差別をする最低な店員がいます。
I went to this restaurant with my Asian friends. I visited because the website menu showed an “omakase aburi sushi” option, which I was interested in trying. However, when we arrived, it was not available on the actual menu.

I asked a male staff member about it, and he told me that if we requested it, the chef could prepare an omakase with some aburi (seared) sushi. When the female server came over, I explained that we would like to order omakase with aburi sushi. She asked which pieces we wanted to be seared, which was reasonable. However, when I asked, “Which sushi pieces would normally be selected?” because it was omakase, she did not check with the chef or try to help. Instead, she replied bluntly, “It’s omakase,” and left it at that.

The restaurant was not busy at all — there were only two other tables occupied — yet this server repeatedly came back almost every minute asking if we had decided what to order. The constant pressure, combined with her unfriendly attitude, made the experience very uncomfortable.

As a Japanese person, I found this level of service especially disappointing from a restaurant that presents itself as serving Japanese cuisine. I believe staff should have a better understanding of Japanese dining culture, especially the meaning of “omakase,” where customers trust the chef’s selection.

The most frustrating part was that when we paid using a certain service, her attitude suddenly changed. She became friendly, smiled, and even asked us to leave a review. So here I am, leaving an honest one.

Unfortunately, the sushi itself was not good, and the sushi was not prepared by a Japanese chef. In my opinion, this felt more like a fake representation of Japanese sushi rather than an authentic sushi experience.
